title: Bipartite Graphs and the Odd-Cycle Criterion
quickIdea: Two colours suffice exactly when no cycle has odd length, and that one criterion decides bipartiteness, the chromatic number of 2, and the maximum-edge formula n squared over 4.
remember: G is bipartite when V splits into two parts and every edge crosses between them; equivalently G has no cycle of odd length.
A bipartite graph with at least one edge has chromatic number 2; with no edges it has chromatic number 1.

Bipartiteness is decided by one BFS or DFS pass: colour the source 0, alternate colours, and report failure when an edge joins two vertices of the same colour, which is Theta(|V| + |E|) on an adjacency list and optimal.
K_{m,n} has mn edges, so a bipartite graph on n vertices has at most floor(n squared / 4) edges, reached by K_{floor(n/2), ceil(n/2)}.
Every tree is bipartite, and so is every acyclic graph; a graph may have cycles and still be bipartite, as long as every cycle is even.
A d-regular bipartite graph has a perfect matching, and its edges split into d perfect matchings.

example.prompt: A bipartite graph has 12 vertices. What is the maximum number of edges, and can the extremal graph contain an odd cycle?
example.work: floor(12 squared / 4) = 36, reached by K_{6,6} with 6 x 6 = 36 edges. K_{6,6} is bipartite by construction, so every cycle alternates between the two sides and has even length.
example.answer: 36 edges, and the extremal graph has no odd cycle.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2014 Set 2 Q.3 is the n squared over 4 formula as a NAT, and GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.45 pairs the odd-cycle criterion with the Theta(V+E) test. Both follow from the same theorem, so one card covers both.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: What is the maximum number of edges in a bipartite graph on 9 vertices?
variations.why: The parts must be as equal as possible, so they have 4 and 5 vertices and the edge count is 4 x 5.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: A graph on 8 vertices has 16 edges and no triangle. Must it be bipartite?
variations.answer: No. Being triangle-free is weaker than having no odd cycle.
variations.why: A 5-cycle is triangle-free and not bipartite, and the Petersen graph is triangle-free on 10 vertices with 15 edges and is not bipartite.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A connected bipartite simple graph on 7 vertices has 12 edges. Is that possible, and what is it?
variations.answer: Yes, and only as K_{3,4}: floor(49/4) = 12 is the maximum, and a bipartite graph that attains it must be complete bipartite.
variations.why: Any missing edge between the two sides could be added, so an extremal bipartite graph is complete bipartite.

trap.what: Calling a graph bipartite because it has no triangle, and answering 1 for the chromatic number of a bipartite graph that has edges.
trap.why: Odd cycles of length 5, 7 and beyond also break 2-colourability, and a single edge already forces two colours.
trap.counterexample: The Petersen graph is triangle-free and has 5-cycles, so it is not bipartite; K_{2,2} has edges and chromatic number 2.

check.question: Is a 6-cycle with one chord joining opposite vertices bipartite?
check.answer: Yes. The chord splits the cycle into two cycles of length 4.
check.explanation: Label the cycle 1 to 6 and add the chord 1-4. The two cycles are 1-2-3-4-1 and 1-4-5-6-1, both of length 4, so every cycle is even and a 2-colouring exists: 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1 around the cycle still separates the ends of the chord.

sourceLine: Bipartite graphs, the odd-cycle criterion, the 2-colouring test and the n squared over 4 bound: GATE Overflow GO Classroom deck (English, read in part) for the bipartite and 2-chromatic statements; Rosen ch. 10 for the extremal formula. Standard references used to verify, never copied: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, ch. 10; West, Introduction to Graph Theory (Brooks, Dirac, Koenig, chromatic polynomial); CLRS ch. 22 (articulation points, bridges) and ch. 26 (bipartite matching); Diestel, Graph Theory (Menger). The odd-cycle criterion and the edge bound are recomputed in scripts/validate.py over every graph on up to 5 vertices.
